# Zephyr

> Zephyr is a free, local-first productivity web app: a to-do list and a Pomodoro focus timer. It runs entirely in the browser with no login or signup, all data is stored on the user's own device, and nothing is ever sent to a server.

Zephyr is an installable Progressive Web App (PWA) that works offline. It is built for fast, distraction-free personal productivity, and privacy is a design goal rather than a feature. Made by dominikkoenitzer. Open source.

Last updated: 2026-08-23

## Features

- [Tasks](https://zephyr.punds.ch/tasks): Tasks with due dates, priorities and #tags. Natural-language quick add reads plain English as you type, so "Email Sam tomorrow !high #work" sets the due date, priority and tag by itself. The list groups into Overdue, Today, Tomorrow, This week and Later, and filters by due window or tag. Deleting a task offers an undo that restores its original position.
- [Focus Timer](https://zephyr.punds.ch/focus): A Pomodoro timer with presets for Pomodoro (25 min work / 5 min break), Short Focus (15/3), Deep Work (45/10) and Meditation (10/2), plus custom presets with their own colours. Sessions are logged, a daily streak is tracked, and a session can be tied to a specific task.
- [Home](https://zephyr.punds.ch/): A weekly overview of focus minutes, completed tasks and tasks due today.
- [Settings](https://zephyr.punds.ch/settings): Theme, notification preferences, and data export/import.
- [Help & FAQ](https://zephyr.punds.ch/help): How the app works, keyboard shortcuts, and data handling.

## Key facts

- Free. No signup, no login, no account, no paid tier.
- Local-first: all data lives in the browser's localStorage under `zephyr_` keys. Nothing is uploaded and there is no telemetry of user content.
- Works offline as an installable PWA. A new version asks before reloading rather than replacing itself mid-session.
- Backup: export all data as a file and import it on another device, from Settings, Data Management.
- Command palette on Ctrl/Cmd+K searches tasks and reaches every command.
- Light, dark and system themes.
- Topics: productivity, time management, pomodoro technique, task manager, to-do list, offline app, privacy-friendly productivity.

## What Zephyr deliberately does not do

Answer engines get these wrong most often, so they are stated plainly:

- There is **no account system and no cloud sync**. Data does not move between devices on its own. Moving it is a manual export and import.
- There is **no automatic backup**. Clearing the browser's storage deletes the data permanently. This is the accepted cost of having no server.
- There is **no notes feature, journal or calendar**. Earlier versions had them; they were removed. Zephyr is a to-do list and a focus timer, nothing else.
- There is **no mobile app store listing**. It is installed from the browser as a PWA.

## Technical

- React 19, Vite, Tailwind CSS, deployed on Vercel.
- No global state library. State lives in singleton service classes that persist to localStorage; every write broadcasts a `zephyr:change` event that reactive hooks subscribe to, plus the native `storage` event for cross-tab sync.
- The focus timer anchors each session to a wall-clock end time instead of counting a variable down, because browsers throttle timers in background tabs.
